mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate indicates tight monetary conditions, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of periods when UNRATE is below 5%, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong demand in the housing market, which spills over into broader economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of periods when HOUST is increasing, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests strong supply-side activity, which supports economic growth and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of periods when INDPRO is increasing, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low unemployment and high payroll employment signals a strong labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of periods when UNRATE is below 5% and PAYEMS is increasing, this hypothesis is rejected.
